questions.prompt: How many main scripts are mixed together in written Japanese?
questions.explain: Hiragana, katakana and kanji.

questions.prompt: What is the main official language of Iran?
questions.explain: Persian is also called Farsi.

questions.prompt: Arabic is written from right to left.
questions.explain: Arabic, like Hebrew, is read from right to left.

questions.prompt: The word 'kindergarten' comes from which language?
questions.explain: It means 'children's garden'.

questions.prompt: The word 'tsunami' comes from which language?
questions.explain: It means 'harbour wave'.

questions.prompt: The word 'robot' comes from which language?
questions.explain: It was introduced in Karel Čapek's 1920 play R.U.R.

questions.prompt: The word 'algebra' comes from which language?
questions.explain: It comes from al-jabr, in a book by al-Khwarizmi.

questions.prompt: The English word 'shampoo' comes from which language?
questions.explain: It comes from the Hindi word chāmpo, meaning to press or massage.

questions.prompt: A sentence that uses every letter of the alphabet is called a…
questions.explain: 'The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog' is a famous pangram.

questions.prompt: Which is the most commonly used letter in written English?
questions.explain: E appears in about one in eight letters of English text.

questions.prompt: What is the main language spoken in the Canadian province of Quebec?
questions.explain: French is Quebec's only official language.

questions.prompt: Which country has the most native Spanish speakers?
questions.explain: Mexico has over 120 million Spanish speakers.

questions.prompt: What is the official language of Egypt?
questions.explain: Arabic replaced Coptic as the main language centuries ago.

questions.prompt: Basque is not known to be related to any other living language.
questions.explain: Basque is a language isolate, spoken in Spain and France.

questions.prompt: What is the plural of 'crisis'?
questions.explain: Words ending in -is from Greek often change to -es: one thesis, two theses.

questions.prompt: Which language is the main language of Brazil?
questions.explain: Brazil was a Portuguese colony.

questions.prompt: What does the abbreviation 'e.g.' stand for?
questions.explain: 'i.e.' is id est, 'that is'.

questions.prompt: What does 'etc.' stand for?
questions.explain: Et cetera is Latin for 'and the rest'.

questions.prompt: Which part of speech describes a noun, like 'big' or 'green'?
questions.explain: Adjectives describe nouns; adverbs describe verbs.

questions.prompt: What is the name of the alphabet used to write Russian?
questions.explain: Cyrillic is also used for Bulgarian, Serbian and others.

questions.prompt: What is the fastest bird in a dive?
questions.explain: A diving peregrine can top 300 km/h.

questions.prompt: What is the only mammal capable of true flight?
questions.explain: Flying squirrels and colugos glide; only bats truly fly.

questions.prompt: How many hearts does an octopus have?
questions.explain: Two pump blood through the gills and one through the body.

questions.prompt: What is a group of crows called?
questions.explain: A parliament is owls, a gaggle is geese, a pod is dolphins.

questions.prompt: What is a baby swan called?
questions.explain: A gosling is a baby goose.

questions.prompt: What is a male honeybee called?
questions.explain: Drones' main job is to mate with a queen.

questions.prompt: What does a koala mostly eat?
questions.explain: Koalas sleep up to 20 hours a day to save energy.

questions.prompt: Which of these mammals lays eggs?
questions.explain: The platypus and echidnas are the only egg-laying mammals.

questions.prompt: Snakes use their tongues to smell.
questions.explain: The tongue collects scent particles and passes them to an organ in the mouth.

questions.prompt: Dolphins can sleep with one half of their brain at a time.
questions.explain: This lets them keep surfacing to breathe.

questions.prompt: A shark's skeleton is made of cartilage, not bone.
questions.explain: Cartilage is the same flexible material as in your ears.

questions.prompt: Starfish do not have a brain.
questions.explain: They have a ring of nerves instead of a central brain.

questions.prompt: Bats are blind.
questions.explain: All bats can see; many also use echolocation.

questions.prompt: Goldfish have a memory of only three seconds.
questions.explain: Studies show goldfish can remember things for months.

questions.prompt: What is the largest living reptile?
questions.explain: Big male saltwater crocodiles can exceed 6 m long.

questions.prompt: What is the largest living lizard?
questions.explain: Komodo dragons can grow to 3 m long.

questions.prompt: What is the largest species of cat?
questions.explain: Siberian tigers can weigh over 300 kg.

questions.prompt: Which animal is the longest-lived vertebrate known?
questions.explain: Some Greenland sharks are estimated to be several hundred years old.

questions.prompt: Camels store water in their humps.
questions.explain: Humps store fat, which camels can use for energy.

questions.prompt: Bees make honey from which part of flowers?
questions.explain: Bees turn sugary nectar into honey in the hive.

questions.prompt: Which animal has the largest eyes in the animal kingdom?
questions.explain: Its eyes can be about 27 cm across.

questions.prompt: Hummingbirds can fly backwards.
questions.explain: They are the only birds that can truly fly backwards.

questions.prompt: The kiwi bird is native to which country?
questions.explain: The kiwi is a flightless bird and a national symbol.

questions.prompt: A rhino's horn is made of bone.
questions.explain: Rhino horns are solid keratin, like hair and nails.

questions.prompt: Coral is a plant.
questions.explain: Corals are animals: colonies of tiny creatures called polyps.

questions.prompt: Which animal is known as the 'ship of the desert'?
questions.explain: Camels can go days without drinking.

questions.prompt: Which bird lays the largest eggs?
questions.explain: An ostrich egg weighs about 1.4 kg.

questions.prompt: What is a group of owls traditionally called?
questions.explain: The name comes from owls' reputation for wisdom.

questions.prompt: Which animal has black and white fur and lives in the mountains of central China?
questions.explain: Wild giant pandas live in bamboo forests in China.

questions.prompt: Which insect is famous for its 'waggle dance'?
questions.explain: The dance tells other bees where to find food.

questions.prompt: How many legs does a lobster have?
questions.explain: Lobsters are decapods, which means 'ten legs'.

questions.prompt: What is the process by which plants make food from sunlight?
questions.explain: Photosynthesis turns light, water and carbon dioxide into sugar.

questions.prompt: What green pigment helps plants capture sunlight?
questions.explain: Chlorophyll reflects green light, which is why leaves look green.

questions.prompt: What is the tallest species of tree?
questions.explain: The tallest known redwood is about 116 m tall.

questions.prompt: Which plant has the largest single flower in the world?
questions.explain: Its flower can be about 1 m across and smells of rotting meat.

questions.prompt: Mushrooms and other fungi are plants.
questions.explain: Fungi are a separate kingdom, more closely related to animals than plants.

questions.prompt: The Venus flytrap catches and digests insects.
questions.explain: Its leaves snap shut when trigger hairs are touched.

questions.prompt: Bamboo is a type of tree.
questions.explain: Bamboo is a giant grass; some kinds can grow almost a metre in a day.

questions.prompt: What type of cloud usually brings thunderstorms?
questions.explain: Cumulonimbus clouds can tower over 10 km high.

questions.prompt: What does an anemometer measure?
questions.explain: Many anemometers use spinning cups.

questions.prompt: Lightning is hotter than the surface of the Sun.
questions.explain: A lightning bolt can reach about 30,000 °C, around five times hotter than the Sun's surface.

questions.prompt: What are hurricanes called in the north-west Pacific Ocean?
questions.explain: In the Indian Ocean they are called cyclones.

questions.prompt: You can tell a tree's age by counting the rings in its trunk.
questions.explain: Most trees in places with seasons add one ring each year.

questions.prompt: Trees that lose all their leaves each year are called…
questions.explain: Oaks and maples are deciduous.

questions.prompt: Which part of a plant takes in water from the soil?
questions.explain: Roots also anchor the plant in the ground.

questions.prompt: What is the name for an animal that is active mainly at night?
questions.explain: Owls and bats are nocturnal.

questions.prompt: What is the name for animals that are active mainly at dawn and dusk?
questions.explain: Rabbits and deer are often crepuscular.

questions.prompt: What is the hard outer layer on a tree trunk called?
questions.explain: Bark protects the tree.

questions.prompt: What is the name for a scientist who studies fungi?
questions.explain: An entomologist studies insects; an ornithologist studies birds.

questions.prompt: What is a scientist who studies insects called?
questions.explain: Herpetologists study reptiles; ichthyologists study fish.

questions.prompt: Which gas do plants give off during photosynthesis?
questions.explain: Almost all the oxygen in the air comes from photosynthesis.

questions.prompt: Who created Mickey Mouse?
questions.explain: Disney created him with animator Ub Iwerks.

questions.prompt: Mickey Mouse first appeared in theatres in which 1928 cartoon with synchronised sound?
questions.explain: It premiered in New York in November 1928.

questions.prompt: What was Disney's first full-length animated feature film, released in 1937?
questions.answer: Snow White and the Seven Dwarfs
questions.explain: Pinocchio and Bambi followed in the 1940s.

questions.prompt: What is the name of Superman's home planet?
questions.explain: Superman was sent to Earth as a baby before Krypton exploded.

questions.prompt: In which city does Batman fight crime?
questions.explain: Metropolis is Superman's city.

questions.prompt: What is Spider-Man's real name?
questions.explain: Peter Parker first appeared in 1962.

questions.prompt: What is the name of Wonder Woman's home island?
questions.explain: It is home to the Amazons.

questions.prompt: Who wrote the Harry Potter books?
questions.explain: The first book was published in 1997.

questions.prompt: Which Hogwarts house is Harry Potter sorted into?
questions.explain: Gryffindor's emblem is a lion.

questions.prompt: In 'Star Wars', who is Darth Vader's son?
questions.explain: Vader reveals the truth in The Empire Strikes Back (1980).

questions.prompt: In 'The Lord of the Rings', who forged the One Ring?
questions.explain: Sauron forged it in the fires of Mount Doom.

questions.prompt: What is Sherlock Holmes's famous address?
questions.explain: Holmes shared the rooms with Dr Watson.

questions.prompt: What is James Bond's code number?
questions.explain: The '00' means he has a licence to kill.

questions.prompt: Who created James Bond?
questions.explain: The first Bond novel, Casino Royale, came out in 1953.

questions.prompt: What is the name of Tintin's dog?
questions.explain: In the original French he is called Milou.

questions.prompt: Asterix belongs to which ancient people?
questions.explain: Asterix's village holds out against the Romans.

questions.prompt: What is the name of Mario's brother in Nintendo games?
questions.explain: Luigi is the taller brother in green.

questions.prompt: What job is Nintendo's Mario best known for?
questions.explain: Mario and Luigi are the Super Mario Bros., plumbers from Brooklyn.

questions.prompt: How many ghosts chase Pac-Man in the original arcade game?
questions.explain: Blinky, Pinky, Inky and Clyde.

questions.prompt: In which country was Tetris created?
questions.explain: Alexey Pajitnov created it in Moscow in 1984.

questions.prompt: What type of Pokémon is Pikachu?
questions.explain: Pikachu stores electricity in its red cheeks.

questions.prompt: Minecraft was first created by a developer from which country?
questions.explain: Markus 'Notch' Persson released the first version in 2009.

questions.prompt: What colour is Sega's Sonic the Hedgehog?
questions.explain: Sonic first appeared in 1991.

questions.prompt: The Rubik's Cube was invented by a professor from which country?
questions.explain: Ernő Rubik invented it in 1974.

questions.prompt: How many pieces does each player start with in chess?
questions.explain: 8 pawns, 2 rooks, 2 knights, 2 bishops, a queen and a king.

questions.prompt: Which chess piece can jump over other pieces?
questions.explain: The knight moves in an L shape.

questions.prompt: How many squares are on a chessboard?
questions.explain: An 8 × 8 grid.

questions.prompt: In which town do The Simpsons live?
questions.explain: The show began in 1989.

questions.prompt: What is the name of the Muppets' famous frog?
questions.explain: Kermit was created by Jim Henson in 1955.

questions.prompt: In 'The Wonderful Wizard of Oz', what is the name of Dorothy's dog?
questions.explain: L. Frank Baum's book was published in 1900.

questions.prompt: What is the name of the Doctor's time machine in 'Doctor Who'?
questions.explain: It looks like a 1960s police box.

questions.prompt: Who was captain of the starship Enterprise in the original 'Star Trek' series?
questions.explain: The original series began in 1966.

questions.prompt: How many cards are in a standard deck, not counting jokers?
questions.explain: Four suits of 13 cards.

questions.prompt: On a standard die, opposite faces always add up to seven.
questions.explain: 1 is opposite 6, 2 opposite 5, and 3 opposite 4.

questions.prompt: In the 1933 film, which New York building does King Kong climb?
questions.explain: The Empire State Building had opened in 1931.

questions.prompt: Who directed the 1997 film 'Titanic'?
questions.explain: It won 11 Academy Awards.

questions.prompt: Who directed the 1960 thriller 'Psycho'?
questions.explain: Hitchcock was known as the 'Master of Suspense'.

questions.prompt: In 'Wallace & Gromit', what kind of animal is Gromit?
questions.explain: Gromit never speaks but says a lot with his eyebrows.

questions.prompt: In which country was the LEGO toy company founded?
questions.explain: LEGO comes from the Danish 'leg godt', meaning 'play well'.

questions.prompt: What colour is the Hulk?
questions.explain: The Hulk first appeared grey in 1962 before becoming green.

questions.prompt: Which country does paella come from?
questions.explain: Paella comes from Valencia.

questions.prompt: What is the main ingredient of guacamole?
questions.explain: Guacamole comes from Mexico.

questions.prompt: Which herb is the main ingredient of traditional pesto?
questions.explain: Pesto alla genovese comes from Genoa, Italy.

questions.prompt: The spice saffron comes from which plant?
questions.explain: Saffron threads are the dried stigmas of the crocus flower.

questions.prompt: Botanically, a tomato is a fruit.
questions.explain: A fruit grows from a flower and contains seeds.

questions.prompt: Peanuts are a kind of tree nut.
questions.explain: Peanuts are legumes that grow underground in pods, like peas and beans.

questions.prompt: Lightning never strikes the same place twice.
questions.explain: Tall buildings like the Empire State Building are struck many times every year.

questions.prompt: The colour red makes bulls angry.
questions.explain: Bulls can't see red well; they react to the movement of the cape.

questions.prompt: Ostriches bury their heads in the sand when frightened.
questions.explain: They lower their heads to tend eggs or hide, but they don't bury them.

questions.prompt: Napoleon Bonaparte was unusually short for his time.
questions.explain: He was about 1.69 m, roughly average for a Frenchman of his era.

questions.prompt: Viking warriors wore horned helmets into battle.
questions.explain: No horned Viking battle helmet has ever been found; the idea came from 19th-century costume designs.

questions.prompt: Albert Einstein failed maths at school.
questions.explain: Einstein excelled at maths and had mastered calculus by about 15.

questions.prompt: Old window glass is thicker at the bottom because glass slowly flows.
questions.explain: Glass is an amorphous solid; uneven old panes come from how they were made.
